subject: Post-call qualification: MedAlign model-fit playbook + dataset schema
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Leah Park <lpark@medalign.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: model-fit recommendations + eval pack (next steps)

Thanks Leah — great call earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Summary of what we heard
- Primary use case: automated summarization + clinical extraction for intake notes (high precision on ICD-like labels + concise patient-safety summary)
- Target latency: 200–300ms token time for interactive reviewer UI; batch/async throughput okay for nightly runs
- Data sensitivity: PHI-containing notes; customer needs on-prem or VPC run, SOC2/audit proofing

Redwood recommendations (initial)
- Models to evaluate: Llama-2-13B (float16) for best quality baseline; Redwood-3B (int8 quantized) for cost/latency tradeoff; GPT-JT-8B for a lightweight alternative on longer context
- Eval surface: extraction F1 for structured labels, top-3 span accuracy for entity localization, and a human-reviewed quality score for summaries (1–5)
- Minimum pass criteria to consider pilot: extraction macro-F1 >= 0.82 and summary human score >= 4.0

Attached: medalign_eval_prompts_v1.csv (sample prompt bank) and scope matrix PDF.

What we need from MedAlign to run an initial Redwood-hosted eval (can also run in your VPC during next phase)
1) 200–400 de-identified sample notes (CSV) with columns: id, note_text, ground_truth_labels (JSON), expected_summary (optional)
2) Confirmation on allowed redaction/sanitization approach (we can accept partial PHI masking)
3) Which routes you want measured: interactive vs batch

Next steps (proposed)
- Leah: share a small sample by EOD Wed (6/16) — drop into the Drive link below or send secure upload
- Ben + Karthik: prepare an evaluation config and runner on Redwood, including scoring harness and regression guards
- Schedule a 60-min technical workshop (suggest Tue 6/22 or Wed 6/23) to align on scoring edge cases and security posture

I’m looping in Ben and Karthik for the technical specifics below. Let me know if anything above is incorrect or missing.

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: RE: Post-call: model-fit recommendations + eval pack (next steps)

Quick technical plan to respond to Leah's questions and prepare the eval runner: 

1) Data format (what we will accept for the initial run)
- CSV with columns: id, note_text, ground_truth_labels, expected_summary, context_metadata (optional)
- ground_truth_labels: JSON string with schema {"entities": [{"label":"ICD10","start":12,"end":21,"value":"E11.9"}, ...]}

2) Models & recommended config (for lab runs on Redwood-hosted; VPC ops similar but will use dedicated infra)
- Llama-2-13B (fp16): batch_size=8, max_tokens=1024, expected median token-latency ≈ 220ms on p4-equivalent with continuous batching
- Redwood-3B (int8): batch_size=16, max_tokens=1024, median token-latency ≈ 120ms — good cost/latency trade for reviewer workflows
- GPT-JT-8B: choose for long context cases (>2k tokens), expect ~300ms token-latency, but better recall on long-range extraction

3) Scoring & regression controls
- Automated metrics: extraction precision/recall/F1 (macro + micro), span IoU for entity boundaries, ROUGE-L for summaries
- Human checks: random 2% manual review per run to validate hallucination risk and summary fidelity
- Regression gating: block model promotion if extraction macro-F1 drops by >3% vs baseline or human summary score drops by >0.25 points

4) Security & hosting notes for Leah
- Hosted smoke run: we can run a one-off evaluation in Redwood-hosted infra with full-at-rest encryption and audit logs; we will not store raw notes beyond temporary execution and will provide the audit log export
- VPC/private: next phase; we will provide deployment packaging and an operator runbook (KMS integration, HSM optional)

5) Deliverables for next week
- Evaluation config (JSON) + scoring harness for the three model candidates
- A short tech notes doc explaining token-latency numbers under typical load

Related artifacts: Redwood eval runner: https://app.redwood.ai/evals/run/D-8462

I’ll draft the config and push to the Drive folder; Marissa, can you confirm the workshop date you want to propose?

—Ben
